chunks: Sa'd narrated from Ahmad, from Ali ibn Hadid and Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurarah, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the Prayer of Fear and the Traveler's Prayer, are both shortened? He said, 'Yes, and the Prayer of Fear is more deserving of being shortened than the Traveler's Prayer, because there is no fear in it.'
ai.seo_question: Is the Prayer of Fear shortened more than the Traveler's Prayer?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Baqir (AS) clarifies the hierarchy of prayer shortening, establishing that Salat al-Khawf (Prayer of Fear) takes precedence over Salat al-Safar (Traveler's Prayer) due to the added dimension of danger. This ruling reflects the Shia jurisprudential principle that greater hardship or distinct circumstances warrant more lenient rulings, distinguishing the immediate threat of battle or fear from the general fatigue of travel. The hadith underscores the flexibility of Islamic worship in adapting to varying levels of physical and spiritual strain.
